name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v2195: Locking in the vault arc after a cross family review of it returned six findings. A vault write that failed used to report that the vault already had it, because one else branch covered both the already case and the failure case, so a refusal wore a success sentence in the one surface that exists to verify. There are three outcomes and three sentences now, and a refusal says REFUSED and carries the reason. A failure mid sweep was silent and indistinguishable from a name that was already vaulted, while earlier names in the loop had already been written and nothing recorded that anything went wrong, which over hundreds of names is a half filled vault reported as a clean run; failures are carried out on the receipt with their reason. The receipt counted a newly vaulted name in both the skipped and the vaulted buckets without saying so, so the counters measured two different ledgers and looked contradictory; the overlap is named explicitly, because skipped has always meant the grail did not move and that must stay true. A no op registration cost a dictionary write for every already vaulted name over hundreds, so the common case is an in memory lookup now, which also shrinks the window where a quota failure can stop the loop half way. Four guards were added for those, and one of them was wrong at first in an instructive way: it seeded a name into the vault and the page load time accept list REBUILT the vault from its catalogues and replaced it, so the test was measuring its own fixture rather than the code. It uses a name the rebuild keeps.
